title: Chapter 121: Sleepwalking?
html:
Something had possessed Wang Haiming inside the psychiatric hospital and followed him out. The two fought constantly for control of his body, and Wang Haiming had ultimately chosen death over surrender.

His bizarre death and the disturbances at midnight supported Chen Ge’s theory.

After Wang Haiming died, the creature he had brought from the hospital must have remained in Room 303. With police and onlookers surrounding the body, it could not reveal itself, and by nightfall the room had been sealed before it could seek a new host.

The monster should have remained trapped, but by some unknown means, it appeared to have formed a pact with the young man in Room 302. Perhaps it had learned from Wang Haiming and no longer tried to seize its host by force. Instead, the two existed in a kind of symbiosis.

Chen Ge studied the sparrows. These few birds couldn’t have soaked so much fabric with blood. Their pact must have begun long ago.

He recalled the young man shouting, “You all need to stop forcing me.” The words revealed that he was being compelled to act against his will. Judging by Room 303, the monster had probably demanded living sacrifices.

A few sparrows would not satisfy it forever. Soon it might demand stray cats, then dogs—or even people.

More troubling was the phrase “you all.” The young man had used the plural, suggesting he faced more than one entity. What, exactly, had Wang Haiming brought out of the hospital?

After restoring everything, Chen Ge approached the window. Because of the angle, the tenant of Room 302 did not realize he had been spotted. The moment Chen Ge’s shadow drew near, the spy hastily withdrew.

One more person to watch tonight.Chen Ge climbed onto the sill. As he began to turn, a movement at the edge of his vision drew his gaze toward Room 303’s bathroom. Behind the half-open door stood a long shadow with two different faces.

“Who’s there?!” Chen Ge’s hands almost slipped. When he focused his eyes, the thing had disappeared. There was nothing in the bathroom, but a shadow seemed to flash across the mirror.

Dangling three stories above concrete without a safety line, Chen Ge could not afford to linger. He hurried back into Room 304.

“Did you find anything?” Doctor Gao asked out of politeness.

“Look at this.” Chen Ge retrieved the key from his pocket. “Doctor Gao, are there any locks at your hospital that require a key like this?”

Doctor Gao took the unusually large key and turned it over in his hand. “It doesn’t resemble any key used for the offices or operating rooms. I’m not sure.”

Unable to get an answer, Chen Ge put it away. He would test it when he entered the Third Sick Hall.

“That’s all you found? A key?” Doctor Gao ended the call. He had not known what to expect from the excursion, but certainly not this.

“Don’t underestimate it. This key might unlock the whole mystery.” Chen Ge glanced into the bedroom. “Has Men Nan fallen asleep?”

“I don’t think he should sleep in Room 304. The environment frightens him, and that added stress may increase the likelihood of another nightmare.” Concern clouded Doctor Gao’s face. “Now that we’ve traced his condition to childhood trauma, we should focus on counseling him.”

“It isn’t that simple.” Chen Ge answered patiently. Doctor Gao had never encountered the supernatural, so his reasoning could go only so far. “If childhood trauma were the sole cause, why did his condition flare up only after he moved into this apartment?”

Doctor Gao had no answer to that question.

“His childhood trauma is merely what the problem in this apartment is exploiting. Something here triggered the relapse. That is the true source.” Chen Ge explained as much as he could without mentioning the supernatural.

Doctor Gao nodded. He still had doubts about Chen Ge’s methods, but he could not deny that the man had cured Wang Xin. The scientist in him wanted to understand Chen Ge’s theories; the physician cared only whether they helped his patients.

Seeing the hesitation on Doctor Gao’s face, Chen Ge pressed on. “Moving him won’t stop the nightmares—you’ve already tried that. Let him sleep here while we watch him. The instant he shows signs of distress, we’ll wake him.”

Psychological treatment would take time. After considering the proposal, Doctor Gao finally agreed. When they entered the bedroom, they found Men Nan already asleep, exhausted and slumped against the bed with his chin on the pillow.

After getting Men Nan into the bed, Chen Ge wanted to examine Men Nan’s forehead and neck but was stopped by Doctor Gao. “Let him sleep.”

“Okay.” Chen Ge pulled two chairs over. “We’ll do this in rounds. One will stay up until midnight, and the other will take over. Whenever there’s something wrong, we’ll wake him up immediately.”

“You should go and rest for now. Leave this to me.”

Doctor Gao had Chen Ge sleep on the living room sofa while he stayed in the bedroom to look after Men Nan.

After a morning in the Haunted House and an afternoon making mannequin heads, Chen Ge was exhausted. He switched his phone to vibrate, set an alarm for midnight, and soon fell asleep on the sofa with Xiaoxiao beside him.

…

A vibration in his palm pulled him from sleep. Chen Ge sat up and checked his phone. It was midnight.

He entered the bedroom and found Doctor Gao frowning deeply. Before he could speak, the doctor raised a finger to his lips. They waited silently beside the bed. Five minutes later, Men Nan abruptly stiffened his arms beneath him as though trying to push himself upright.

After several failed attempts, his arms collapsed and flopped weakly at his sides, as if the movement itself had been a dream.

“Sleepwalking?” Chen Ge whispered to Doctor Gao. The latter shook his head and pointed at Men Nan’s eyes.

Following Doctor Gao’s finger, Chen Ge saw that Men Nan’s eyes were open, but his pupils had rolled so far upward that only a sliver remained visible.
